title: Shield Island
story: A player keeps treasure safe on a small island while a friendly raider tries to touch the ball.
setup: Create one 7x7-yard island for every pair, with one ball and safe space between islands.
instructions: One player begins with the ball and keeps it inside the island for 20 seconds.
The raider scores by touching the ball with a foot; play continues until time ends.
The player with the ball may turn, stop, change speed or place their body between raider and ball.
Swap roles every round and ask each pair to show one escape they discovered.
coach_lens: Look for players glancing at pressure, keeping the ball on the far side and turning toward open space. Allow experimentation rather than demanding a named turn.
questions: Where can you put your body to keep the ball safe?
What space appears when the raider moves?

simplify: Enlarge the island or let the raider walk.
challenge: Add two small escape gates; dribbling through either ends the round successfully.
low_attendance: Keep pairs; the coach joins an unmatched player.
high_attendance: Add islands rather than placing several raiders around one ball.
limited_equipment: Use existing field lines or four shoes to mark an island.

safety: Use standing foot challenges only; no pushing, grabbing or slide tackling.
Stop the round if the ball enters another pair's island.

diagram.alt: Several small square islands each contain one player shielding a ball from one raider.

source.title: How to help 5-11s develop their skills on the ball
source.reviewer_notes: SmallSide-authored paired game applying England Football guidance on staying on the ball, shielding, turning away from pressure and patient exploration. No source wording or artwork reproduced.
